text:
olivia: quick heads-up — saw a short spike of 502s on /v1/generate around 12:02–12:05 UTC. Rate ~12r/s for ~3m, p95 latency also up. Can someone drop the dashboard + trace links and a suggested quick triage checklist? @oncall FYI :eyes:

samir: put these together — Grafana panel for ingress errors: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd/ingress-errors?var-route=%2Fv1%2Fgenerate (time range auto).
Kibana logs query (nginx-ingress):
```
service:nginx-ingress AND route:\"/v1/generate\" AND status:[500 TO 599]
```
Trace samples (Jaeger): https://tracing.internal/redwood/search?service=gateway&operation=forward_request&tags.route=%2Fv1%2Fgenerate
Also check kv-cache hit-rate dash: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/efgh/prefix-cache

jun: quick suggestion for alerts — bump the 502 alert from eval_period=1m to eval_period=5m and add `for: 2m` so short bursts don't page. Also add a separate high-rate noisy-4xx rule (>=100rps 4xx) and route-specific 5xx for production traffic.

eng-oncall-bot: ALERT: prod-gateway-502-spike triggered at 1912345598 — 502 rate = 12.1r/s, p99 latency = 1.9s. Pager: none (severity=warning). Incident runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/502-triage

olivia: thanks — can you paste the exact Kibana filter I should use to pull the request_id + upstream response code? the logs are a bit messy in that timeframe.

samir: use this fields filter in Kibana: `request_id: * AND @http.response.status: 502 AND route: "/v1/generate"` — then add columns `request_id, upstream_addr, upstream_status, upstream_time`. If you need a single-sample curl to reproduce a failing path try: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://api.internal.redwood/v1/generate\" -d '{"input":"test"}'` (may need to set X-Request-ID header to correlate).

ops-bot: FYI — we've seen two node reboots in gpux-04 yesterday that correlate with elevated CPU on the gateway. Node events: https://infra.events.internal/nodes/gpux-04/notes

jun: for triage steps: 1) pull Grafana p95/p99, 2) sample 5 traces from Jaeger in the window, 3) grep Kibana for request_id and upstream_status, 4) check gateway logs for 502 cause (upstream timeout vs connection reset), 5) check autoscaler and pod restarts (`kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | grep gateway`). If it's upstream timeout, increase timeout or add fallback.

olivia: got it. I'll collect 5 traces and post a snippet here. Can one of you open a quick PR to change the prod 502 alert window (samir/jun)? I can add the sample traces to the incident note after. :raised_hands:

samir: I'll open the PR to update alerting (will include suggested eval_period=5m & for:2m). Linking PR when ready.

olivia: perfect — thanks. posting first trace now and will follow up with a short postmortem if it recurs.
